statusText: Mapped policy state: EA_ON. Tail is 4, low, because CME equity index futures have been halted since 21:00Z on Friday and no tradable Nasdaq-100 price path exists inside any hour of this 24-hour horizon, which ends about five hours before the scheduled Sunday reopen. Stress is 41, moderate: a 50% US tariff on about $20bn of Canadian goods is in force, Ottawa has suspended talks and dated a dollar-for-dollar match to 8 September, the H.15 curve stands at 4.19% on the 2-year, 4.69% on the 10-year and 5.23% on the 30-year with the long end at its highest since 2007, and next week carries PCE, the second GDP estimate, Nvidia's results and a first Jackson Hole keynote from the current Fed Chair. Confidence is 87, high, because the closed-venue fact is verified and the supporting index, volatility, yield, energy and calendar inputs were all rechecked against primary sources this hour.
recommendation: The last observed session remains consistent with functioning mean reversion rather than a one-way path: cash NDX opened at 29,359.60, traded down to 29,142.44, recovered the entire decline to 29,405.12 and closed at 29,308.86, below its own open and up 0.33% on the day, while VIX settled at 14.89 near the low of a 14.77-15.95 range. Both session extremes were retraced and neither produced repeated extension after a failed pullback, so no Tail amplifier from observed structure is present. Because the venue is shut, no hour in this horizon can generate the shallow-pullback or extreme-holding behaviour that would move Tail toward the block threshold, and Tail therefore stays at its closed-venue floor while Stress carries the unpriced policy and rates stack. The danger window is empty by construction: there is no tradable interval inside the published horizon.
headline: Closed-venue assessment: CME equity index futures stay halted across all twenty-four published hours while a 50% US tariff on Canadian goods meets a matching response dated to 8 September, a 30-year yield at its highest since 2007 sits unpriced, and Tail holds the closed-venue floor of 4.
body: CME equity index futures stopped trading for the week at 21:00Z on Friday and reopen on Sunday at 22:00Z, so the venue is confirmed shut across all twenty-four slots published here, which run from 2026-08-22T17:00:00Z to 2026-08-23T16:00:00Z and end roughly five hours before that reopen. Cash NDX settled at 29,308.86 on Friday, up 95.69 points or 0.33% from a 29,213.17 previous close, after opening at 29,359.60, printing a 29,142.44 low and a 29,405.12 high; both extremes were retraced inside the session and the close finished below the open, which is the shape of a market that still mean-reverts. QQQ closed the same session up 0.35% at 713.44, and VIX closed at 14.89, down 6.00%, near the bottom of a 14.77-15.95 range rather than at a stressed extreme. The dominant unpriced item is trade policy: talks between Washington and Ottawa collapsed shortly before the Friday midnight deadline, a 50% US tariff on roughly $20bn of Canadian goods took effect, and Prime Minister Carney suspended negotiations while dating a dollar-for-dollar response to 8 September, outside this horizon. The rates backdrop is the second unpriced item: the latest H.15 column shows 4.19% on the 2-year, 4.69% on the 10-year and 5.23% on the 30-year, with the long end at its highest level since 2007 after a week in which the S&P 500 and the Nasdaq Composite both finished lower. Energy remains a background channel, with WTI near $87.06 after a second consecutive weekly gain of about 5% while Strait of Hormuz transit volumes stay reduced. Delayed cross-asset context from the shared collector is consistent with the last session rather than with any live path: index futures marginally higher, VIX futures softer, gold firmer and Treasury futures lower across the curve, with five of eight megacaps positive and semiconductors mixed. None of these is a price path, so none of them raises Tail. The published Tail therefore holds 4 in every slot, the mapped policy state stays EA_ON, and Stress traces a shallow 39-44 path that eases through the quiet overnight hours and rebuilds toward the reopen as PCE, the second GDP estimate, Nvidia's results and the Jackson Hole keynote come into view.

lookbackSummary: Claude coverage over the past 24 hours is close to complete: 22 hourly assessments are available, while the 05:00Z and 06:00Z clock-hours on 22 August have no published assessment and are marked unavailable. Across the available hours Tail held a narrow 4-16 band and the mapped policy state stayed EA_ON throughout, so no hour approached the block threshold. The path tracks the transition from the live Friday session, where Tail ran 13-16 and Stress 53-54 with a mixed dominant mode, into the futures halt at 21:00Z, after which Tail fell to the closed-venue floor of 4 and the dominant mode settled to normal. Stress fell with the halt to 35-36 overnight and then rebuilt to 42 through Saturday as the tariff step took effect, easing to 41 in the most recent hour once the Canadian response was dated to 8 September. Confidence stayed in an 84-88 band throughout.
outlookSummary: The current hour carries Tail at 4 because CME equity index futures are confirmed halted and no Nasdaq-100 price path can develop inside this slot. All twenty-three remaining slots describe the same closed market: the final slot begins at 2026-08-23T16:00:00Z and ends about five hours before the Sunday 22:00Z reopen, so no live evidence can arrive before this forecast expires. Tail therefore holds 4 in every hour and the mapped policy state stays EA_ON, with the danger window empty because no tradable interval exists inside the horizon. Stress eases from 41 to 39 through the quiet Saturday evening and overnight hours, then rebuilds to 44 by the final slot as the reopen approaches with the tariff step, a 2007-high long end, the unresolved Iran campaign and next week's PCE, GDP, Nvidia and Jackson Hole checkpoints all still unpriced. Confidence decays from 87 to 81 across the horizon purely because the last live price observation ages, not because any source degraded.
